item.title: PlayStation Founder Understands Why Players Want to Keep Physical Media Alive
item.description: Ken Kutaragi, PlayStation founder and former Sony chairman, has voiced his opinion on a hot topic in the gaming community: the end of physical media. As a businessman, Kutaragi believes that there is no reason to continue disc production, but he understands why gamers are upset about it.

item.title: 'Avatar: Seven Havens' Creators Officially Reveal What Inspired the Devastated New World
item.description: One of the clearest artistic touchstones is French comic artist Jean Giraud, better known as Moebius, whom Avatar creator Bryan Konietzko mentioned as inspiration for the new series on stage at New York Comic Con 2026. Arzach and other works, particularly his contributions to the sci-fi anthology magazine Métal Hurlant , helped establish a visual language for alien worlds that feel simultaneously desolate and brimming with fascinating cultures. Moebius frequently anchored his frames with solitary figures set against colossal landscapes, letting strange architecture and alien terrain tell the story without leaning on heavy exposition. This same philosophy feels central to Seven Havens , where the wilderness is much more than a mere obstacle for Pavi and Nisha to overcome; it’s a standing monument to a deep and lost history that predates them entirely.

item.title: New Fortnite Season Might Not Be One Piece After All, New Official Ads Reveal
item.description: With the end of Chapter 7 Season 4 on the horizon, rumors had begun spreading regarding the theme of the upcoming Fortnite mini-season. Beloved manga and anime series One Piece was the most popular contender, especially after a mysterious pirate chest appeared on the island. Epic Games has begun putting up promotional posters, and the design suggests that the mini-season might just have a generic anime theme rather than being an exclusive One Piece crossover.

item.title: 5 Best Halloween 'Peanuts' Comics That Don't Involve the Great Pumpkin
item.description: Halloween in Charles Schulz's Peanuts frequently meant it was time for another run at the Great Pumpkin . This running gag, introduced in 1959, was sort of like Schulz's answer to Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot . Linus van Pelt spent every Halloween for almost 40 years waiting for the Great Pumpkin to arrive, and he never did.

item.title: 3 Video Games Where Your Choices Actually Make a Difference
item.description: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game? Typically, we think it's a good use of branching narratives when you have a properly big, dramatic effect on how things play out or when you have hundreds of endings. Just look at how so much attention on Baldur's Gate 3 focused on its endings or, years before, how everyone tended to ignore the smaller ways the Mass Effect trilogy changed across three games in favor of looking at the restrictive outcomes in Mass Effect 3 .

item.title: 'Red Dead Redemption' 2 Mod Is 'Shadow of Mordor' Meets the Wild West
item.description: The Lord of the Rings games Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor and Shadow of War introduced the Nemesis system, a mechanic that makes enemy orcs remember encounters with the player, develop rivalries and return seeking revenge. The system helped set the games apart by turning random encounters into personal vendettas that could evolve over time.

item.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Adventure Games that are Barely Playable Today
item.description: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4 Is Legitimately a Top-5 Call of Duty Campaign
item.description: Infinity Ward has long been the Call of Duty studio to rely on for single-player campaigns. The original Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare and Modern Warfare 2 are still the best in the whole series, and the reboot got off to a strong start with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare in 2019. Despite a slightly underwhelming runtime, Modern Warfare 4 , the latest, is up there with the very best of them.

item.title: Stupid Never Dies Is Easily the Worst Game of 2026
item.description: Dated doesn’t begin to describe the debut action RPG from GPTRACK50, a new studio founded by former Capcom producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi. Style points only count for so much in a downright regressive action game that’s saddled with a supremely uncomfortable story, a repetitive faux-roguelike hook, and unresponsive combat that wastes some good RPG depth. It’s the kind of game I might have loved as a kid with a low bar for quality, and one that I’d have to make a lot of excuses for loving as an adult who knows better.

item.title: Street Fighter Officially Sets a New Franchise Box Office Record
item.description: For nearly 40 years and across six mainline entries — plus dozens of spinoffs and rereleases — Street Fighter has been one of gaming's most enduring franchises. But adaptations of the magical martial arts source material have proven tricky, with previous attempts garnering mixed reception from fans and critics.
